posts.body_html:
What happens when you cross the two best clones in the collection with each other? yes, yes...you've heard the answer before ladies and gentlemen....bliss.....pure bliss!

Here's montana best clone Transylvania Co, NC for reference:
farm6.staticflickr.com/5573/14971278747_f7bf30b1c0_c.jpg

and here's the henderson Co, NC montana: sarracenia.proboards.com/thread/5838/sarracenia-montana-henderson-nc

These seedlings haven't reached their fullest potential in terms of shape and color, they tend to be "chameleons" and not look as incredible when small compared to plants that have reached vegetative maturity, but with a keen eye lots of Sarr NURDZ know these are all winners! I expect some more pronounced "bulbosity" aka bulbousness as these get bigger:

posts.body_html:
couple more pics. I think what's very important to explain here is phenotypic plasticity: clones that produce very bulbous traps at maturity can look quite boring when they are juveniles. Case and point: check out the most bulbous rosea clone I have in the collection, I didn't even know it was special for many years because it looked like this:


Pretty amazing, right? Nope! BUT.....here's the EXACT same clone at vegetative maturity, straight up holy grail level of bulbousness!


Same thing happens with montana ladies and gentlemen! These montana (best clone x henderson Co, NC) seedlings aren't yet bulbous, but both parents are and most of these are expected to have some incredible, round shapes as they mature. That said, they're still pretty darn beautiful even as seedlings:




the bulbous outline is already there in many of them!
